title: Matrix Sketching for Online Analysis of LCLS Imaging Datasets
problem: X-ray light source facilities generate massive high-dimensional data streams at high repetition rates that require real-time analysis to inform ongoing experiments. The high dimensionality and speed make both scalable and interpretable analysis of beam profile and detector data challenging.
motivation: Enabling fast feedback-driven analysis of streaming detector data is essential for optimizing experiment steering and beam quality monitoring at scientific facilities.
method: The system processes X-ray detector data in three stages. First, it compresses each incoming batch using ARAMS, a sketching algorithm that combines Priority Sampling (selecting the most informative measurements) with a modified Frequent Directions algorithm (extracting the main patterns in the data). The compressed data is then reduced to fewer dimensions using PCA, visualized using UMAP, and grouped into clusters using OPTICS. All three stages run in parallel across multiple processors, enabling real-time analysis as data arrives.
key_novelty: ARAMS enables rank-adaptive matrix sketching by combining Priority Sampling with a modified Frequent Directions algorithm, letting practitioners specify target error tolerance instead of choosing how many key patterns to keep upfront.
contributions: Parallel image monitoring and classification framework for real-time analysis of streaming scientific instrument data
ARAMS algorithm enabling rank-adaptive matrix sketching with user-specified error targets
Demonstration of real-time analysis capability on LCLS beam profile and diffraction datasets
Strong empirical performance and scalability results for streaming data analysis

metrics.other: empirical performance and scalability on LCLS datasets

primary_theme: real-time streaming data analysis via matrix sketching
